report_title: Final commitment: exact binary-auxiliary projection and certified redundancy removal

shape.source: 48,950 vars (all integer) / 98,021 rows (10,861 E, 87,160 L, 1 N OBJ) / 292,875 constraint nonzeros / 17,578,329 B MPS; bounds 46,502 [0,1], 1,044 [-1,0], 60 [0,4], 16 [0,8], 1,316 fixed 0, 12 fixed 1; identically zero objective
shape.target: 31,482 vars / 71,479 rows (11,065 E, 60,414 L) / 194,147 constraint nonzeros; target.mcm 8,866,589 B from source.mcm 12,870,525 B

edit_summary: 16,140 private binary auxiliaries, each occurring in exactly two pairwise-disjoint inequalities and nowhere else, are projected out: their 32,280 source rows become 42,768 exact local relations before dedup (13,056 forbid-exactly-two with 3 rows, 1,496 implication, 772 at-least-one, 612 equality, 192 forbid-exactly-one, 12 unrestricted), 26,544 exact duplicate rows are dropped to a keeper, 10,486 rows are dropped with bound-interval certificates, and 1,328 isolated fixed variables are dropped and restored at their fixed values. Zero objective unchanged.

rpa_text_census_measured.note: token counts over cases/test74/proof.rpa; the Cases count equals kernel statistic branches=257120

claims: Claim 0 (reverse=false): 31,482-entry projection map source->target; obligations are 2 bound checks plus integrality per target variable, one Le/Eq per target row (71,479), the zero objective Eq and one Eq per retained coordinate; the 16,224 surviving replacement rows are discharged by local case trees handed in the rows dict, the rest by source row premises.

Claim 1 (reverse=true): 48,950-entry map; the 16,140 eliminated auxiliaries map to bounded Boolean conjunctions of at most seven retained bits or their complements (4,532 distinct conjunctions in one IntervalLift wave), the 1,328 fixed coordinates map to constants; one check per source row (98,021) plus bounds and integrality per variable.
Both claims: input_integers=output_integers=true, objective='Equal', inverse=None, no point/LP-equality/optimality claim; auxiliary reconstruction is explicitly not claimed globally unique.
request.json is exactly the two claims (854,051 B): 2 x 31,482 index pairs plus six scalar fields per claim, i.e. the retained map is re-listed by hand for each direction.
Kernel outcome: VERIFIED exit 0, 473,762 obligations, 257,120 branches, work 37,545,628 of 1e9 (3.75%), depth 9 blocks, 2 byte-identical re-verifications.
proof_encoding: RPA 7 text (prepare_test72.write_rpa, tools/prepare_test72.py:384) written by tools/prepare_test74.py:156-158 through execute(); proof.rpa 196,090,550 B -> proof.rpx 109,356,997 B, assemble 1.41 s, verify 1.25 s.
Measured census of the delivered text: 257,120 'Cases' nodes (= kernel branches), 596,916 'EqPair', 439,423 'Lin', 36,484 'Int' and exactly one 'IntervalLift' - the branch trees dominate the bytes.

Each local relation is proved by bounded_cases (tools/prepare_test74.py:36-56): a Cases tree over the at-most-seven retained bits, each branch pruned only by an explicit Lin bound-combination certificate; leaves emit Lin constants the kernel recomputes.

The 4,532 distinct conjunctions become free interval variables with lower/upper extension rows and pairwise bound cross-checks (checked_intervals, tools/prepare_test72.py:293), then and_integer (tools/prepare_test74.py:78-93) proves EqPair+Int that the conjunction is exactly 0/1.

Duplicate handling is proof-side: every replacement row name is first walked to its keeper through audit duplicate_rows (keeper, tools/prepare_test74.py:25-29) so both directions cite one retained row.
agent_manual_work: Read the whole 17.6 MB MPS with a purpose-written exact parser (sections, marker state, RHS/bounds uniqueness, Fraction arithmetic) because no framework code reads a model.

Enumerated the truth table of every one of the 16,140 auxiliaries by hand (123,344 assignments x both auxiliary values) and classified six relation families; the constructing eval cell was interrupted by the 30 s timeout (digest:693).

Recomputed whole-model facts: column-degree scan, pairwise disjointness of the 32,280 source rows, bound-interval redundancy over all 98,021 rows (10,498 hits), exact row-signature dedup (30 original pairs, 26,544 after projection).

Wrote an 11.8 MB free-format MPS plus a 16.8 MB audit.json (schema 'exact-binary-projection-audit-v1'), then a second, independent 179-line verifier that re-parses both files and re-checks every assignment, bound certificate, duplicate certificate and restoration.
Turned all of it into report prose and artifacts by hand: 19 turns, 18 tool calls, 1 failing call, 408.5 s wall.
preparer_helpers: decision(d) (:13-20) brute-forces a conjunctive completion over at most seven literals, with complement, that matches the audited allowed set - the only map from a truth table to a reconstruction term.
bounded_cases (:36-56) re-implements prepare_test72.exhaustive (:51) with pruning and per-literal value overrides; it produces the 257,120 branch nodes.
and_integer (:78-93) builds the EqPair+Int 0/1 proof of a conjunction, and reverse() (:99-107) dedups the 4,532 conjunctions and lays them out as one IntervalLift wave via checked_intervals.
forward (:58-76) and reverse (:95-148) are the per-direction emitters, each re-expanding the same local bit scope; 130 of the file's 159 lines are these emitters.

replacement_owner/keeper (:23-34) resolves duplicate chains by hand with a cycle assert, and prepare (:151-154) hand-builds the two claims, the 31,482-pair projection list, the counts and the contract string.
friction: Text is the binding resource, not work: 196,090,550 B = 73.05% of the 256 MiB RPA limit while work is 3.75% of the 1e9 budget; nothing in the API predicts bytes or offers a cheaper encoding.

The same local scope is re-expanded per row and per direction: 257,120 Cases nodes for 16,140 local scopes. The sibling test75 delivers 1,102,643 obligations in 37,269,768 B (34 B per obligation against 414 B here).
The audit contract is untyped: raw key lookups (h['projections'], :98), a linear scan per leaf for the allowed values (:120), duplicate chains walked by hand with a self-written cycle guard (:25-29).

Obligation bookkeeping is manual: 62,964 of the 473,762 obligations are coordinate identities emitted as real checks, the same 31,482 pairs are re-listed in the 854,051 B request, and claim 1 is claim 0's reverse yet both carry inverse=None.

The library boundary is by case name: tools/prepare_test74.py imports four sibling preparers (:7-10) and calls emit_checks from prepare_test48, so an edit to any of them silently alters this certificate.
